findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, colliding across anonymous, render, user, and service-account subjects
findings.body: In `Check`, `permDenialKey` is constructed with `userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...)`, where `checkReq.UserUID` is the ID portion extracted by `types.ParseTypeID( req.GetSubject())` without the identity type prefix. Both `"anonymous:0"` and `"render:0"` parse to `checkReq.UserUID == "0"`, and `"user:<id>"` and `"service-account:<id>"` share the same `UserUID` when numeric IDs are used. If an anonymous request (`"anonymous:0"`) is denied `dashboards:read`, `folders:read`, or `datasources:read` on a resource, `permDenialCache` records a denial under `<ns>.perm_0_<action>_<name>_<folder>`. Subsequent `Check` calls for the render service (`"render:0"`) within the 30s TTL will hit `permDenialCache` and return `Allowed: false`, even though the render service is granted wildcard read permissions in `getRendererPermissions`. Include the identity type (or full subject) in `userPermDenialCacheKey` (and/or skip `permDenialCache` for `TypeRenderService`).

findings.title: Non-cache-miss errors from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` cause duplicate `GetUserIdentifiers` DB queries
findings.body: `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)` for `TypeUser` and `TypeServiceAccount`, which queries the database when the user identifier is not in `idCache`. If `GetUserIdentifiers` returns an error (e.g., the user does not exist or the DB fails), both `Check` (line 124) and `List` (line 181) treat any non-nil error as a cache miss and immediately call `s.getIdentityPermissions`, which calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers` a second time for the same user. `Check` and `List` should only fall back to `getIdentityPermissions` when `errors.Is(err, cache.ErrNotFound)` and return other errors immediately.

findings.title: Denial cache test sets `permCache` entry to `false` instead of `true`
findings.body: In `TestService_CacheCheck` (`"Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"`), line 982 sets `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}` in `s.permCache` with the comment `// Allow access to the dashboard to prove this is not checked`. Because the map value is `false` (and `fakeStore` has no permissions), `checkPermission` would return `false` even if `permDenialCache` were never consulted. The map value should be `true` so the test actually verifies that `permDenialCache` overrides an allow in `permCache`.
